AuthnLoginActionResult.description: The answer of a flow that finished by binding an external identity (`linked`) or registering a factor (`enrolled`); neither issues a session or a token.

state.description: linked when the flow bound an external identity; enrolled when it registered a factor

AuthnLoginAnswer.description: One of four shapes, told apart by `state` and the members present: an open flow, a completed login delivered as a session, a completed login delivered as a token pair or an elevated step-up, or the result of a link or enrollment.

AuthnLoginFactor.description: One second factor the flow offers to verify: its identifier, its kind and a display label. It carries nothing secret.

id.description: The factor's identifier; send it as `input.factor` when answering the second-factor step.

kind.description: The factor kind, such as `totp`, `sms` or `webauthn`; the client renders the challenge according to it.

label.description: A display label for the factor; it may be empty, in which case the client falls back to the kind's own name.

AuthnLoginField.description: One input a method asks the client for, named by the method and rendered according to its kind.

kind.description: How the client renders the input: `text`, `password`, `code` or `phone`.

name.description: The input's key: the client submits its value under this name in the `input` map of the start request or of the answer.

required.description: Whether the step needs a value; absent means the field may be left out.

secret.description: Whether the value must not be displayed or echoed, as for a password or a code; absent means it is not secret.

AuthnLoginFlow.description: One open login flow, as returned by a start, by an answer that keeps the flow open, or by the current-flow read: the step number the next answer must echo, the flow's state, the flow token when the flow is bound by the header, and what the client does next.

flow_token.description: The flow token, set only when the flow is bound by the Authn-Flow header

next.description: What the client does at the flow's current step.

seq.description: The step number the next answer must echo

state.description: The flow's state: first, second, enroll, ready, processing, done or failed

AuthnLoginHuman.description: The human-verification gate a deployment puts in front of every send of a verification message: whether a proof is required, the mechanism that checks it, and the public identifier a client-side widget needs. A deployment that takes no gate in reports the off mechanism and requires nothing.

provider.description: The mechanism that checks a proof: `off` when no gate is configured, `pow` for the self-hosted proof of work, or `turnstile`

required.description: Whether every send of a verification message must first present a valid, single-use proof

site_key.description: The public identifier a client-side widget is rendered with, for a mechanism that needs one; absent for `off` and `pow`

AuthnLoginIdentifierState.description: The answer of adding an identifier: `added` when the identifier is written, `pending` when a code was sent to an email address and the answer is still to come. The two durations are present only in the pending state.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds; absent when the state is added

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds; absent when the state is added

state.description: added when the identifier is written; pending when a code was sent to an address and its answer is still to come

AuthnLoginMFA.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, as the multi-factor module reports them. This is a deployment-level list, not the caller's own registered factors.

factors.description: The kinds of second factor the deployment takes in

AuthnLoginMethods.description: The discovery document of the login surface: one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off, whether registration is open, the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in, and the human-verification gate this deployment requires before a verification message is sent. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

human.description: The human-verification gate a send must satisfy.

methods.description: The methods taking part that are not turned off, one descriptor each, sorted by name

mfa.description: The second-factor kinds the deployment takes in.

password_reset.description: Whether this deployment offers the anonymous password reset, and the channels it may use.

signup.description: Whether registration is open on this deployment: true when either `authn.account.signup` or `authn.account.password-signup` is `open`.

AuthnLoginPasswordReset.description: Whether this deployment offers the anonymous password reset and through which channels. It is a deployment fact, the same for every anonymous caller, and it says nothing about whether any account can be reset.

enabled.description: Whether the anonymous password reset is open: the switch is open, the audit record is present, and at least one channel is available

methods.description: The channels the reset may be sent through: email and sms, sorted, leaving out a channel that is not assembled, whose template is missing or that a disabled method turned off

AuthnLoginPasswordResetState.description: The state of the bound anonymous password reset: whether a code was sent or the identifier is proved, how long the code or the proved ticket lives, and, while a code is outstanding, how soon another may be asked for. It carries no account, no identifier and no code.

expires_in.description: How long the code or the proved ticket lives, in whole seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in whole seconds; absent once the identifier is proved

state.description: sent after a code was sent, verified once the code held

AuthnLoginPhoneChallenge.description: The answer to a phone-verification send: how long the code lives and how soon another code may be asked for, both in whole seconds. It carries neither the challenge identifier nor any fact about whether the number is already held by another account.

expires_in.description: How long the code lives, in seconds

resend_after.description: How soon another code may be asked for, in seconds

AuthnLoginRegistration.description: The answer of an anonymous self-registration: the state name `registered`, the account that was opened, and the email address awaiting verification. No session is made and no email is sent.

account_id.description: The identifier of the account that was opened

state.description: The literal `registered`, marking that an account was opened

AuthnLoginRegistrationContact.description: The contact a new registration has to prove: the pending state of the email address the caller gave, which is not yet a login name.

email.description: The email address the caller gave, awaiting verification

state.description: The verification state of the email address: `pending` until the address is proved after signing in

AuthnLoginSession.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=session`, and of a step-up completed on a cookie session: the state name `authenticated` and the public facts of the session that was created or elevated. The session cookie is set in the same response.

session.description: The public facts of the session the login created.

state.description: The literal `authenticated`, marking a completed login.

AuthnLoginSessionView.description: The public facts of the session a login created. No token or secret is included.

expires_at.description: The session's expiry as an RFC 3339 instant, or empty

id.description: The session identifier; the browser client holds the session cookie written in the same response.

AuthnLoginSignup.description: Whether anonymous self-registration is available on this deployment: either a first login may open an account, or the name-and-password register route is open. The two switches are independent; each member below reports its own.

enabled.description: Whether anonymous self-registration is available: true when either a first login may open an account or the name-and-password register route is open

password.description: Whether the name-and-password register route is open.

AuthnLoginSignupPassword.description: Whether the anonymous name-and-password register route is open, reported on its own because it is independent of a first login opening an account.

AuthnLoginStep.description: What the client does at the flow's current step. Only the members that belong to `kind` are present: `challenge` carries `fields`; `redirect` carries `url` and `method`; `factor` carries `factors`; `enroll` carries `kinds`; `webauthn` carries `options`; `complete` carries nothing.

expires_in.description: How long a challenge lives, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

factors.description: The factors a second-factor step offers

fields.description: The inputs a challenge step asks for

kind.description: What the client does next: challenge, redirect, factor, enroll, complete or webauthn

kinds.description: The factor kinds an enroll step takes in

method.description: The HTTP method the redirect uses

options.description: The data a webauthn step carries: the public-key creation or request options of a WebAuthn ceremony, or, for a TOTP enrollment, an object with an `otpauth_uri` the client renders as a QR code.

resend_after.description: How soon a challenge may be asked for again, in seconds. No handler of this fragment sets it, so the member is absent from every answer.

url.description: Where a redirect step sends the user agent

AuthnLoginToken.description: The answer of a login completed with `delivery=token`, and of a token-delivered step-up: the state name, the token type, the access token, its lifetime and the refresh token.

access_token.description: The access token, sent in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer <value>`.

expires_in.description: The access token's lifetime in seconds

refresh_token.description: Empty on a step-up, which issues no refresh token

state.description: authenticated for a login; elevated for a step-up, which issues no refresh token and carries it empty

token_type.description: The authorization scheme the access token is sent with; it is always `Bearer`.

AuthnMethodDescriptor.description: One login method as the discovery document reports it: its stable name, how a client renders it, the protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks, its brand label, whether it can open an account, the provider values its bindings appear under, and the inputs its first step asks for.

binding_providers.description: The stored provider values, or namespace prefixes, the method's bindings appear under; absent means the method's name

fields.description: The inputs the method's first step asks for, empty for a method that does not open with a form

kind.description: How a client renders the method: form, redirect, enterprise or webauthn

label.description: The method's brand name where it has one, otherwise empty for a name-keyed translation

opens_account.description: Whether the method may open an account for an identifier it does not yet know; false for the phone and social methods when `authn.account.signup` is closed

protocol.description: The wire protocol a redirect or enterprise method speaks: oauth2, oidc or saml; empty otherwise

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Handles a provider's callback as a top-level browser navigation. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a navigation cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so a replayed authorization code or assertion loses the compare-and-swap and gets 401 flow-invalid. A GET callback that carries no flow cookie is always 401 flow-invalid: an identity-provider-initiated sign-in is served only as a POST. A cookie login that completes on this route answers 303 to the flow's stored return target instead of a body. A token-delivery login whose request declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) answers 303 the same way, with no session made and the flow left at ready; without that declaration it is answered the completion body. A callback of a purpose other than login (a link, or a step-up of an account with no factor) that reaches ready answers 303 the same way, with no session made: the flow stays in the cookie at ready for the host's callback page to read with `GET /auth/flows/current` and complete with `POST /auth/flows/answer`.

parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.
parameters.name: provider

200.description: The flow, advanced by the callback, as answered to an API callback: a token-delivery login whose callback declares no navigation. A login that declares a navigation is answered 303 instead.

303.description: The user agent is sent to the flow's stored return target instead of being answered a body: a completed cookie login writes its session cookie in this response, a token-delivery login whose callback declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) keeps the flow cookie at ready and makes no session, a flow that still needs a second factor or an enrollment keeps the flow cookie and resumes with `GET /auth/flows/current`, and a callback of a purpose other than login that reached ready keeps the flow cookie the same way and completes through `POST /auth/flows/answer`. When the flow recorded no return target, the configured `authn.login.default-return-to` is used.

Location.description: The flow's stored return target, or the configured `authn.login.default-return-to` when the flow recorded none.

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state: a completed link names an external identity another account already holds

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

get.summary: Handle a provider's callback as a browser navigation

post.description: Handles a provider's callback delivered as a cross-site form post, which is how SAML's assertion consumer service is reached. The callback is bound through the flow cookie only, because a form post cannot set a request header; the path's provider must equal the provider recorded in the flow and the flow must be at its first factor, otherwise the call is a 401 flow-invalid before any method is asked. The posted form is bounded to 512 KiB before it is parsed, and a body over that bound is answered 401 login-failed with the flow left a tombstone. The engine moves the flow to processing before calling the method, so an assertion is handled at most once. A token-delivery login whose request declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) answers 303 to the flow's stored return target with no session made and the flow left at ready; without that declaration it is answered the completion body. A callback of a purpose other than login (a link, or a step-up of an account with no factor) that reaches ready answers 303 to the flow's stored return target, with no session made and the flow left in the cookie for the host's callback page to read with `GET /auth/flows/current` and complete with `POST /auth/flows/answer`. Without a flow cookie the route serves an identity-provider-initiated sign-in, but only for an enterprise provider whose row enables it.

parameters.description: The provider this callback is for: a social method's stable name, or, for an enterprise SSO provider, the identifier the start named in `input.provider`. It must equal the provider recorded in the flow the callback is bound to; a mismatch is a 401 flow-invalid and the callback never reaches a method.
parameters.name: provider

200.description: The flow, advanced by the callback, as answered to an API callback: a token-delivery login whose callback declares no navigation. A login that declares a navigation is answered 303 instead.

303.description: The user agent is sent to the flow's stored return target instead of being answered a body: a completed cookie login writes its session cookie in this response, a token-delivery login whose callback declares a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`) keeps the flow cookie at ready and makes no session, a flow that still needs a second factor or an enrollment keeps the flow cookie and resumes with `GET /auth/flows/current`, and a callback of a purpose other than login that reached ready keeps the flow cookie the same way and completes through `POST /auth/flows/answer`. When the flow recorded no return target, the configured `authn.login.default-return-to` is used.

Location.description: The flow's stored return target, or the configured `authn.login.default-return-to` when the flow recorded none.

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state: a completed link names an external identity another account already holds

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

post.summary: Handle a provider's callback as a cross-site form post

post.description: Starts a login flow for the method named in the body and advances it through the method's first step. The flow token is written to the flow cookie, or, with `binding` set to `header`, returned in `flow_token` with no cookie; later calls are bound to the flow by that token. The route reads no cookie, so a stale session cookie does not prevent a login. Depending on the method and the multi-factor policy, the returned flow may already stand at a second-factor, enrollment or ready step. A body that is not `application/json` is a 415, an unknown member or a value outside its domain is a 400, and a credential the method did not accept is a 401 login-failed — except two refusals the route answers as a 400: a phone prefix the deployment does not allow (`unsupported-region`) and an identifier that cannot name an account (`bad-request`). A 429 carries `Retry-After` when the back-off states a delay.

schema.description: The start request; `method` must name a login method this deployment takes in, or the call is a bad request.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`, or `authn-flow` when insecure use is allowed) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

delivery.description: How a completed login is delivered: `session` (the default) sets the session cookie and answers the session view; `token` answers an access and refresh token pair. `token` must be enabled by the deployment and requires the token capability, otherwise the request is a 400 bad-request.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the method's first step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes; anything beyond is a 400 bad-request.

method.description: The stable name of a login method, as returned in `name` by `GET /auth/methods`. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request; a method turned off by the deployment is a 403 method-disabled.

purpose.description: Accepted but not read by this route: a flow started here always has the purpose login. Use `POST /auth/flows/authenticated` for link, step-up or enroll.

return_to.description: Where the callback lands the user agent: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts; anything else is a 400 bad-request. The callback lands the user agent there for every purpose that reaches ready: a login, a link and a no-factor step-up. An absent or empty value uses the configured `authn.login.default-return-to`, which is held to the same rule and falls back to `/`. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

requestBody.description: The start request: the method to run, how the flow token is carried, where to return after a completed login, and the fields the method's first step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

200.description: The flow, advanced to its first step

400.description: The body could not be read, a value is outside its domain, or the method refused the identifier as a region the deployment does not serve (`unsupported-region`) or as one that cannot name an account (`bad-request`)

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable, or a human-verification proof is missing or invalid (human-verification-required)

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.
Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

post.summary: Start a login flow for one method

post.description: Advances the flow the request is bound to by one step. The body must echo the flow's current `seq`, or the call is a 401 flow-invalid. `step` must be one of `answer`, `factor`, `enroll` or `complete`: a name outside that set is a 400 bad-request, and a step the flow's state does not accept is a 401 flow-invalid. A flow accepts at most eight client answers, after which it is moved to failed and every later answer is a 401 flow-invalid. The answer is the flow at its next step or, once the flow is ready, the completed result: the session view, the token pair, or the `linked`/`enrolled` result of a link or enrollment. Each step is a compare-and-swap on the flow record, so concurrent answers are decided by the store and the loser gets 401 flow-invalid rather than a retry.

schema.description: One answer to the bound flow: which step is being answered, the step number to echo, and the fields the step takes.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the step takes, as name-to-value strings. At most 8 members, each value at most 8 KiB; a second-factor step reads `factor` to choose the factor and then the values that factor asks for, an enrollment step reads `kind`, and `complete` reads nothing.

seq.description: The `seq` of the flow as last returned. It must equal the record's current step number; a stale or future value is a 401 flow-invalid.

step.description: The step being answered: `answer` for a first-factor submission, only while the flow is at the first factor; `factor` for a second-factor step, only at the second factor; `enroll` for an enrollment step, only at the enroll state; `complete` to take the result of a ready flow. A name outside this set is a 400 bad-request, and a step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid.

requestBody.description: One answer to the bound flow: the step number to echo, the step being answered, and the fields that step takes. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

200.description: The flow advanced, or completed with a session or a token pair

400.description: The body could not be read, or a value is outside its domain

401.description: The credential did not hold, or the flow binding is missing or wrong

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable, or a human-verification proof is missing or invalid (human-verification-required)

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state: a completed link names an external identity another account already holds. A step that does not match the flow's state is a 401 flow-invalid, not a 409.

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.
Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

post.summary: Answer the current step of the flow the request is bound to

post.description: Starts a `link`, `step-up` or `enroll` flow on the identity the gateway authenticated and advances it to its first step. The flow is bound to the effective account and the caller's session: an impersonating identity starts it for the impersonated account and proves its own factors. A link and an enrollment require the fresh authentication the effective account's factors call for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise — and answer 401 insufficient_user_authentication with `WWW-Authenticate` when it does not hold. A step-up whose account holds at least one factor usable for this session starts at the second factor and answers the offered factors without calling the method; an account that holds factors but none usable for this session — because each was activated at or after the session authenticated — is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication, and an account with no factor starts at the first factor with the method named in the body. The delivery mode is not read from the body: it follows the kind of the request's session.

schema.description: The start request for a purpose other than login; `purpose` must be `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`.

binding.description: How the flow token is carried: `cookie` (the default) writes the flow cookie (`__Host-authn-flow`, or `authn-flow` when insecure use is allowed) and returns no token in the body; `header` returns the token in `flow_token` and sets no cookie, so the client must send it in the `Authn-Flow` request header on every later call. A callback navigation cannot set a header, so a flow bound this way cannot finish a redirect method.

delivery.description: Accepted but not read: the delivery mode follows the kind of the request's session. It is accepted so that a client may send this route the same start body it sends to `POST /auth/flows`.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification message: a Turnstile token or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

input.description: The fields the started step takes, as name-to-value strings: the method's first step for `link`, the enrollment step for `enroll` where `kind` names the factor kind, and nothing for a step-up that starts at the second factor. At most 8 members, each value at most 512 bytes.

method.description: The method to run for `link`, and for a `step-up` of an account that holds no factor. For an enrollment it is not read, and for a step-up the policy answers with usable factors it is not read either; a step-up whose account holds factors but none usable for this session is refused with 401 insufficient_user_authentication before the method is consulted. A name the deployment does not take in is a 400 bad-request.

purpose.description: Required, and one of `link`, `step-up` or `enroll`: bind an external identity, strengthen the current session, or register a factor. Any other value, including an empty one, is a 400 bad-request.

return_to.description: Where the callback lands the user agent: either a path starting with a single `/`, not `//`, without backslash, control characters or `@` and at most 2048 bytes, or an absolute URL whose origin the deployment trusts; anything else is a 400 bad-request. The callback lands the user agent there for every purpose that reaches ready: a login, a link and a no-factor step-up. An absent or empty value uses the configured `authn.login.default-return-to`, which is held to the same rule and falls back to `/`. The value is stored in the flow record, and no parameter of the callback request can change it.

requestBody.description: The request to start a link, step-up or enrollment flow: the purpose, the method and fields where the purpose takes them, how the flow token is carried, and the return target. The body must be `application/json`, is limited to 64 KiB, and refuses unknown members.

200.description: The flow, advanced to its first step

400.description: The body could not be read, or a value is outside its domain

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The method or the account is unavailable, or a `purpose=link` flow is refused because the caller has an email address that is not proved (contact-required), or a human-verification proof is missing or invalid (human-verification-required)

409.description: The request conflicts with the account's state

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.
Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

post.summary: Start a flow on the identity already signed in

delete.description: Removes the flow the request is bound to and clears the flow cookie. The flow token is read from the cookie or the `Authn-Flow` header. A request with no binding, with a wrong binding, or naming a flow that is already gone is answered the same 401 flow-invalid, while a request that removes a live flow answers 204; no session, token or account state is touched.

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong, or the flow is gone

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, when the back-off states a delay; absent otherwise.

delete.summary: Abandon the flow the request is bound to

get.description: Reads the flow the request is bound to so a client can resume it, for example after a page refresh or after a callback sent the user agent back. The flow token is taken from the flow cookie or the `Authn-Flow` header, and a flow bound by the header gets it echoed in `flow_token`. A missing or mismatched binding, and a flow that is done, failed or gone, are all answered 401 flow-invalid. The reply is built from the stored record alone, so a first-factor step the method named cannot be re-prompted with its fields and its `next.kind` is `challenge`.

200.description: The flow's current step, so a page refresh can resume

401.description: The flow binding is missing or wrong, or the flow is done or gone

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

429.description: Too many attempts; retry after the stated delay

post.description: Adds one login identifier to the caller's account. `kind=username` writes a login name at once, recorded as the account's own assertion; `kind=email` sends a code to the address and answers `state: pending` with how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, and the address is written only after `POST /auth/identifiers/verify` accepts the code. A second code to the same normalized address within the resend interval is a 429 throttled; the window is held against the address and shared across sessions and accounts. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for; a write rotates the caller's session token and revokes the account's other sessions. A login name or address another account holds is a 409 conflict, and a deployment with no email channel answers the email branch with 503 unavailable.

human_proof.description: The human-verification proof the deployment may require before it sends a verification code to an email address: a Turnstile token or a proof-of-work token. It is ignored when the deployment requires none or the kind is username. A value longer than 8 KiB is a 400 bad-request before any provider is asked; a missing or invalid proof is a 403 human-verification-required and no message is sent.

A username is NFKC-normalized and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is 3 to 64 characters of [a-z0-9._-] beginning with a letter or a digit and does not carry the reserved static-credential prefix; the stored value is the normalized one. An email address is trimmed and lowercased first, then accepted only when it is ASCII, contains exactly one `@` with no whitespace, and is at most 254 bytes; anything else is a 400 bad-request.

post.description: Accepts the code sent to an email address being added and, on a match, writes the address as an identifier verified by that code. The pending address and the code's digest are read from the server-side record of the caller's session, so the client submits only the code and cannot choose which address is verified. A missing record, one that names another account, or one that does not parse is a 401 flow-invalid. A wrong code is a 401 login-failed; five wrong codes for one issued code spend the pending verification, and the record also expires with the code's lifetime. On success the record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 200 with `state: added`.

delete.description: Removes one login identifier the caller's account holds. The identifier must be the caller's own: one that does not exist and one that belongs to another account are answered identically as a 400 bad-request, so the route discloses nothing about what another account holds. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for. An account that holds a password credential cannot lose its last username or email address: that removal is a 409 login-identifier-required and changes nothing. An account without a password credential may lose its last login name, and removing a phone number is always allowed; a removal that would leave the account with no password, no proved phone number and no external identity is a 409 last-login-method and changes nothing. Unlike the routes that add a way in, this one does not revoke the caller's other sessions, and it publishes no event of its own: `authn.identifier.changed` is published by the account module on the removal.

delete.description: Unbinds one external identity from the caller's account. The binding must be the caller's own; one that is not, whether it does not exist or belongs to another account, is a 400 bad-request. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for — a multi-factor assurance merely declared by an identity provider does not count. The account module refuses to remove the last way to sign in (409 last-login-method); a way only an identity provider declared does not count as a way to sign in, which is why this route asks for local freshness. On success the call publishes `authn.binding.changed` when the provider is in the event payload's closed set, rotates the caller's session token, revokes the account's other sessions, and answers 204.

get.description: Lists one descriptor per login method that takes part and is not turned off by the deployment, sorted by method name, together with whether registration is open and the second-factor kinds the deployment takes in. It reads no credential and no request body, so every caller gets the same document. A method turned off by the deployment is left out rather than reported with a flag, and the call answers 503 when the settings that decide which methods are off cannot be read. Enterprise identity providers are not listed here; they are discovered through the SSO module.

put.description: Changes the caller's password. The call requires the fresh authentication every change of what proves the account asks for — a fresh local multi-factor when the account holds an active factor, a fresh first factor otherwise. The current password may be empty for an account that signed up through a provider and holds no password; a wrong one is a 401 login-failed, and a new password outside the password module's policy is a 400 bad-request. On success the current session is rotated to a new token, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204 with the new session cookie set. An account that has neither a username nor an email address is refused with 409 login-identifier-required.

post.description: Starts an anonymous password reset for the identifier in the body and sends a code to it, or follows the same path without sending one. A target that is not eligible — unknown, disabled, deleted, without a password or whose identifier is not proved by the requested channel — gets the same 202, the same headers and the same reset cookie as an eligible one. Every send budget overrun suppresses the message and still answers 202; only the originating cookie's own resend interval and the login source-address pre-throttle answer 429. The binding is an independent `__Host-authn-reset` cookie; the login flow cookie is neither read nor written, and no session is made.

post.description: Writes the new password of a reset whose identifier has been proved. It re-reads the reset switch and the channel, re-checks that the account is still eligible, writes the mandatory `authn.password.reset` attempted audit row, then writes the password with the account's own checks inside the write transaction: the account must still be enabled, still hold a password credential, and the proved identifier must still belong to it. A password outside the policy answers 400 bad-request and the reset stays proved, so another password may be tried; an account that is no longer eligible answers 403 password-reset-unavailable. On success every browser and token session of the account is revoked, the reset record is removed and the cookie cleared, and the answer is 204. No session is created, and no factor is touched.

post.description: Checks the code sent to the identifier the bound reset is proving. A real SMS code is checked by the SMS capability; a real email code is compared against the salted digest in the record; a suppressed record compares against a local decoy and never passes. Every failure — a wrong code, an expired code, a suppressed record and this record's used-up attempts — is the same 401 login-failed, and the attempts are counted on the record itself. On a match the record moves to verified and the reset cookie's lifetime is refreshed to the ticket lifetime. A closed reset answers 403 password-reset-closed.

post.description: Sends a verification code to a phone number the caller wants to add to the account, and answers how long the code lives and how soon another may be sent, both in whole seconds. The answer carries no challenge identifier and no hint whether the number already belongs to another account: a number another account holds is sent a code exactly as a free one is, and the conflict surfaces only when the verified number is written. The pending verification is held against the caller's session, so one session has at most one and a later call replaces it. The route is present only in an assembly that takes in the SMS code capability. A key-value store that cannot be read is a 503 before any code is sent; a store that cannot be written after the code went out is also a 503, and the code then cannot be verified.

The number and the challenge are taken from the server-side record of the caller's session, not from the request, so a client cannot choose which number is verified. The number's back-off is checked before the code is compared, so a number in back-off answers 429 without offering the code to a guess; a wrong code is a 401 login-failed and counts against the number, and a correct one clears the back-off. On success the pending record is consumed, the caller's session token is rotated, the account's other sessions are revoked, and the answer is 204. A missing pending record, or one that names another account, is a 401 flow-invalid.

post.description: Opens one enabled account in one transaction from a username, an email address and a password, without a session and without sending an email. The email address is only a contact awaiting verification: it is not a login name until it is proved, which happens after the client signs in through `POST /auth/flows` and adds the address through the account self-service routes. The route reads no cookie and keeps no flow, so it has no binding and no sequence number. It passes the cross-origin check and refuses a body that is not `application/json` with 415 and one over 64 KiB, with an unknown member or with a password the policy refuses with 400. Registration that the deployment has closed, the switch read both here as a pre-check and in the account module's own registration, is a 403 signup-closed; a username already taken is a 409 username-taken; an email address another account has reserved or proved is a 409 email-taken, because the reservation row is inserted in the same transaction and its unique constraint is the arbiter; and the per-source and deployment-wide budgets answer 429 with `Retry-After` when they are exhausted.

schema.description: The anonymous registration request: a username, an email address and a password are required; a display name, a language and a time zone are optional. The email address is only a contact awaiting verification, not a login name.

locale.description: The account's language preference, optional, written to the i18n.locale attribute; a value outside the accepted language domain is a 400 bad-request.

password.description: The password, required, held to the deployment's password policy; a password that violates it is a 400 bad-request.

time_zone.description: The account's time-zone preference, optional, written to the i18n.tz attribute; a value outside the accepted time-zone domain is a 400 bad-request.

username.description: The login name, required. A name already taken is a 409 username-taken; a name that cannot be normalized is a 400 bad-request.
